title: Local complete intersection coordinate algebras on arbitrary affine opens
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $Z$ a scheme over $k$ [def-pc-scheme]. Suppose $Z$ admits an affine open cover $Z=\bigcup_{i\in I} Z_i$, where $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ as $k$-schemes and each $C_i$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra which is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Then for every affine open $W\subseteq Z$, its coordinate ring $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_Z)$, with the $k$-algebra structure induced by $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, is finitely generated over $k$ and is a local complete intersection over $k$. The empty scheme and the zero coordinate algebra are allowed.

source.place: Tag 01UG (lemma-local-complete-intersection), equivalence of (1) and (3), applied also to an affine open; Algebra Tag 00SH (lemma-lci-global), algebra.tex, equivalence of (1) and (2). The assumed affine cover makes Z locally of finite type over k, as required in the first lemma.

proof.text: The affine cover by the $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ makes the structure morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ locally of finite type: every point has a $Z_i$ neighbourhood whose coordinate algebra $C_i$ is finitely generated. Fix $z\in Z$ and choose $i$ with $z\in Z_i$. Applying [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion] to the local-complete-intersection affine scheme $Z_i$ gives that its local ring at $z$ is a complete-intersection local ring. The local ring of $Z$ at $z$ is canonically the same because $Z_i$ is an open neighbourhood, so every local ring of $Z$ has this property.

source.place: Tags 01UG and 01T2: the affine-cover definition of locally finite type and 01UG, (1) implies (3).

proof.text: Let $W\subseteq Z$ be affine open and write $S=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_Z)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] directly to the locally finite type structure morphism $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ from step 1, with affine opens $U=W$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$. It gives that the induced $k$-algebra $S$ is finitely generated. At every point of $W$, its local ring is the local ring of $Z$ at the same point, hence is a complete-intersection local ring by step 1. This also covers $W=\varnothing$, where $S$ is the zero ring.

Apply the algebra part of [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion] to the finitely generated $k$-algebra $S$. Every prime of $S$ is the point of $W$ corresponding to a local ring already identified in step 1, so all localizations $S_{\mathfrak p}$ are complete-intersection local rings. The criterion gives that $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$. If $W$ or $Z$ is empty this is the zero-ring convention in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field].

source.place: Tag 00SH (lemma-lci-global), equivalence of (1) and (2), together with Morphisms Tag 01UG for the local-ring interpretation.

split_report.summary: Split the affine-open locality lemma into three arguments. The cover first gives local finite type and, by the pointwise local-complete-intersection criterion (01UG), complete-intersection local rings on Z. Open restriction preserves those local rings; Tag 01T2 gives finite generation of the coordinate algebra of an affine open W, and Algebra Tag 00SH then gives its local-complete-intersection algebra property. Empty schemes and the zero ring are retained. Maintainer-reader repair: step 2 applies the affine-pair statement directly to Z with U=W, avoiding an extra open-restriction assertion; the new criterion cites the definitions of essentially finite type and prime localization, specifies the k-algebra isomorphism of 00SD, and repairs its final math delimiter.
